question: UP-46 shows that exact-fused step 29 scores better than sparse-selected step 24, but step 29 was never eligible for selection. What should run next?
evidence: UP-45 only evaluated selection checkpoints at steps 0, 12, 24, and 48.
UP-46 evaluated frozen states 24 and 29 under the unchanged objective and found step 29 slightly better on the smooth objective and substantially better on hard recurrent metrics.
The complete UP-45 trajectory already exists, so the checkpoint-scheduling hypothesis can be tested without rerunning optimization.
constraints: Do not rerun or retune the optimizer.
Do not privilege step 29 merely because it looked promising after the fact.
Use the unchanged objective to select before consulting held-out hard capability.

candidates.proposal: Rerun the optimizer with a new checkpoint exactly at step 29 and select it if the hard metrics stay strong.
Change the objective to reward exact fusion so step 29 becomes eligible and preferred.
Replay and score every already-recorded UP-45 trajectory state under the unchanged objective, freeze the selected state, and only then evaluate held-out capability.
Declare step 29 the winner immediately because its hard recurrent metrics already beat step 24.

expected_why: Dense replay tests the checkpoint-scheduling hypothesis without optimizer reruns, post-result privileging, or held-out selection leakage.
